top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) credits one coherent achievement: transparent, design-based local-labour-market evidence on how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, wages and adjustment. The designs have been replicated across countries and refined for over a decade without being overturned, so the live debate is over magnitude and persistence. The attribution is clean because Dorn co-authored the central import-shock papers, and Autor carries the task and polarisation strand. The citation should claim adjustment evidence and not originate the task or skill-premium framework, whose authors include Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane. The cost is that Katz and the long-run education-versus-technology framing are left out, and that is an attribution judgement and not a claim that his merit is lower. P003 (Katz variant) is a defensible second because it rests on the same achievement. P004 is third as a mature, field-creating programme, discounted for weaker cross-country identification, adjacency to the 2024 prize, and Besley's less separable share. P002 is a durable method but has wide credit outside a three-name cap and is closer to a method than a discovery. Any award ranks above no award.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Dorn, Hanson or Katz is apparent from my profile. I co-author with committee members Boppart, Friberg and Krusell, who are not candidates. I am at IIES, where Persson (P004) has long been affiliated. My profile records no co-authorship with him, and P004 is ranked third. My research is near P004 and macroeconomics, so I discount my confidence there. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
